title: Gas-Syringe Kinetics with Marble Chips
learningGoal: Assemble a safe expanding gas-collection path, collect a synchronized carbon-dioxide time series for a controlled marble-and-acid reaction, calculate an initial rate, and identify limits on the evidence.

actions.label: Connect the gas syringe to the delivery tube

interaction.successCue: The gas syringe is connected to the delivery tube.
interaction.invalidCue: Connect the gas syringe to the seated delivery tube.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Connect the gas syringe to the delivery tube.

stateChanges: Attach the gas syringe to the delivery tube so the train can be zeroed and leak-checked before it reaches the flask.

feedback.success: Gas syringe connected; the train is not yet on the flask.
feedback.invalid: Connect the gas syringe to the delivery tube.

actions.label: Zero the gas syringe and record the baseline

parameters.note: Read the syringe barrel and record the starting volume, the barrel capacity, and the smallest graduation you can resolve. The baseline is a student read; nothing assumes the plunger starts at 0.0 mL.

interaction.invalidCue: Read the connected gas syringe before recording its baseline.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Read the gas syringe barrel and record its baseline volume.

prerequisites.label: The gas syringe is connected to the delivery tube.

stateChanges: Record the gas syringe baseline, capacity, and readable graduation.

invalidCases.when: The baseline is assumed rather than read from the barrel.
invalidCases.message: An assumed zero is not a measurement.
invalidCases.recovery: Read the barrel against its graduations and record the value you can resolve.

feedback.invalid: Connect the gas syringe before reading its baseline.

actions.label: Leak-check the connected gas path

parameters.note: Confirm that every connection is secure, the tubing is not kinked, the recorded baseline still stands, and the plunger moves freely. A missing connection invalidates volume evidence; a blocked path creates a pressure hazard. This check happens before the reactants meet and while the flask is still open.

prerequisites.label: The gas syringe baseline is recorded.

stateChanges: Record the leak check, zero check, and expanding pressure-relief path.

invalidCases.when: A stopper, tube, or syringe connection is missing or leaking.
invalidCases.message: The apparatus cannot provide valid carbon-dioxide volume evidence.
invalidCases.recovery: Reconnect the missing component and repeat the leak check.

invalidCases.when: The tubing is kinked or the syringe plunger cannot move.
invalidCases.message: The apparatus could build pressure instead of expanding safely.
invalidCases.recovery: Stop and restore the approved expanding or vented path before adding reactants.

feedback.success: Gas path, plunger travel, and zero are checked.
feedback.invalid: Record the gas syringe baseline before leak-checking the train.

interaction.successCue: Gas path and baseline check recorded.
interaction.invalidCue: Record the connection, baseline, plunger-travel and pressure-relief checks.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Record the leak, baseline and pressure-relief checks for the collection train.

actions.label: Measure the guided acid volume

interaction.successCue: The guided acid volume is measured.
interaction.invalidCue: Use the graduated cylinder to measure the configured acid volume.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Pour the guided hydrochloric acid volume into the graduated cylinder.

prerequisites.label: The gas path and baseline are checked.

stateChanges: Measure 50.0 mL for this guided simulator configuration.

feedback.invalid: Check and zero the gas path before measuring reactants.

actions.label: Transfer acid to the reaction flask

interaction.successCue: The measured acid is transferred to the flask.
interaction.invalidCue: Transfer the measured acid into the reaction flask.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Pour the measured hydrochloric acid into the Erlenmeyer flask.

prerequisites.label: The guided acid volume is measured.

stateChanges: Move the measured acid into the reaction flask.

feedback.success: Acid transferred to the reaction flask.
feedback.invalid: Measure the configured volume before transferring it.

actions.label: Weigh the guided marble sample

interaction.invalidCue: Use the tared watch glass and analytical balance to weigh the marble chips.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Read the analytical balance for the marble-chip sample on the tared watch glass.

prerequisites.label: The acid has been transferred to the flask.

stateChanges: Record 1.30 g of marble chips on the tared watch glass for this guided configuration.

feedback.invalid: Transfer the acid, tare the weighing support, and then record the marble mass.

actions.label: Add the weighed marble chips to the acid

parameters.note: The weighed solid enters the acid while the flask is open. The mass that moves is the mass the balance read and it leaves the chip stock, so a repeated trial consumes fresh reactant. Seal the flask through the verified path immediately afterwards.

interaction.successCue: The marble chips are in the acid; the reaction has started.
interaction.invalidCue: Tip the weighed marble chips into the open reaction flask.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Add the weighed marble chips to the acid in the reaction flask.

prerequisites.label: The gas path and baseline are checked.

stateChanges: Move the weighed calcium carbonate into the acid in the open flask and decrement the chip stock by that mass.

invalidCases.when: Reactants meet before the train is connected, zeroed and leak-checked.
invalidCases.message: Carbon dioxide produced before the path is verified is lost.
invalidCases.recovery: Keep the failed-run record and repeat with fresh reactants after verifying the train.

invalidCases.message: Solid cannot be added through a seated delivery stopper.
invalidCases.recovery: Add the chips to the open flask, then seal through the approved path.

feedback.success: Marble chips added to the acid; seal the flask and start the timer now.
feedback.invalid: Measure the marble-chip mass before initiating the reaction.

actions.label: Seal the charged flask through the verified path

interaction.successCue: The stopper and delivery tube are seated in the flask.
interaction.invalidCue: Seat the delivery stopper in the reaction flask.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Seat the rubber stopper and delivery tube in the Erlenmeyer flask.

prerequisites.label: The weighed marble chips are in the acid.

stateChanges: Seat the already connected, zeroed and leak-checked delivery stopper in the charged flask, keeping the path to the freely moving syringe open.

invalidCases.when: The stoppered reaction vessel has no freely expanding or vented gas path.
invalidCases.message: Do not generate carbon dioxide in a rigid closed system.
invalidCases.recovery: Connect the gas syringe, verify that its plunger moves freely, and leak-check the complete path before sealing the flask.

invalidCases.when: The flask is sealed before the acid and the marble chips are in it.
invalidCases.message: A sealed flask cannot be charged, and sealing early loses the start of the run.
invalidCases.recovery: Charge the open flask first, then seal through the verified path.

feedback.success: The charged flask is sealed through the verified expanding path.
feedback.invalid: Add the acid and the weighed chips to the open flask before sealing it.

actions.label: Synchronize reaction contact and time zero

parameters.note: Use the approved initiation method so marble contacts acid while the checked expanding gas path remains connected. Start the timer at the defined contact event and record the first syringe reading at the configured time zero.

prerequisites.label: The charged flask is sealed through the verified path.

stateChanges: Record the synchronized reactant-contact and time-zero event.

invalidCases.when: Timing begins after the defined reactant-contact event.
invalidCases.message: A delayed time zero biases the early-rate evidence.
invalidCases.recovery: Use fresh configured reactants and repeat the run with timing synchronized to the approved contact event.

feedback.success: Reaction contact, gas collection, and time zero synchronized.
feedback.invalid: Record all controlled quantities before initiating the reaction.

actions.label: Record the guided gas-volume series

prerequisites.label: Reaction contact and time zero are synchronized.

stateChanges: Generate the deterministic simulator gas-syringe readings at 5 s intervals from 0 s to 45 s.

feedback.invalid: Synchronize reaction contact and time zero before recording the series.

interaction.successCue: Timed carbon-dioxide volumes recorded against the syringe graduations.
interaction.invalidCue: Read the gas syringe at each configured sampling time and record the paired value.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Record the timed gas syringe volumes for the guided series.

actions.label: Calculate the guided initial rate

parameters.note: The rate is derived from the recorded series over the configured secant interval. No expected value is stored: the gate is that the timed evidence exists, because a stored answer would be a fabricated measurement rather than a derivation.

prerequisites.label: The guided gas-volume series is recorded.

stateChanges: Calculate the secant slope from 0 s to 15 s and report it in mL CO2/s.

feedback.invalid: Record the guided time series before calculating its early slope.

actions.label: Review evidence limits and repeatability

parameters.note: The displayed series is deterministic simulator output for the stated guided configuration, not a student measurement or a replicate distribution. Physical runs require approved acid settings, fresh reactants, repeated trials, documented syringe resolution, and review of leaks, plunger friction, start-time synchronization, chip-size heterogeneity, marble composition, temperature drift, and mixing. Do not infer a universal rate law or real monument lifetime from this single classroom model.

prerequisites.label: The guided initial-rate calculation is accepted.

stateChanges: Record the simulator provenance, repeatability needs, assumptions, and excluded effects.

feedback.success: Evidence limits and repeatability needs recorded.
feedback.invalid: Calculate the guided initial rate before interpreting its limits.

nodes.title: Connect the gas syringe
nodes.description: Connect the syringe to the delivery tube so the train can be verified away from the flask.
hints: Use the delivery-tube port, not the flask body.

feedback.retry: Connect the syringe to the delivery tube.

nodes.title: Zero the gas syringe
nodes.description: Read the connected syringe barrel and record the baseline before any reactant contact.

validation.label: The gas syringe baseline is recorded.

hints: Record the capacity and the smallest graduation you can read, not just the value.

feedback.retry: Read and record the gas syringe baseline.

nodes.title: Leak-check and zero the path
nodes.description: Distinguish an incomplete connection from a dangerous blocked path, then verify the starting zero.
hints: The syringe plunger must be able to move freely.

feedback.retry: Check connections, plunger travel, and the starting zero.

nodes.title: Measure the guided acid volume
nodes.description: Measure the simulator's stated 50.0 mL configuration; classroom values require teacher direction.
hints: Read the graduated cylinder at eye level in a physical run.

feedback.retry: Measure the configured volume in the graduated cylinder.

nodes.title: Transfer acid to the flask
nodes.description: Transfer the measured acid without starting the marble reaction.

feedback.retry: Transfer the measured acid to the reaction flask.

nodes.title: Weigh the guided marble sample
nodes.description: Use the tared watch glass and balance to record the stated simulator mass.
hints: Confirm the balance is tared with the empty watch glass in a physical run.

feedback.retry: Record the marble mass using the analytical balance.

nodes.title: Add marble chips to the acid
nodes.description: Tip the weighed calcium carbonate into the acid while the flask is still open.

validation.label: The weighed marble chips are in the acid.

hints: Seal the flask through the verified path immediately after contact.

feedback.retry: Add the weighed marble chips to the acid in the open flask.

nodes.title: Seal the charged flask
nodes.description: Seat the verified delivery stopper in the flask only after the acid and the weighed chips are in it.
hints: The flask neck is the stopper snap target.

feedback.retry: Seat the stopper in the flask neck.

nodes.title: Synchronize contact and time zero
nodes.description: Define the contact event and start timing without disconnecting the checked gas path.
hints: Early-rate evidence is sensitive to a late time zero.

feedback.retry: Record the approved contact event and time zero.

nodes.title: Record the gas-volume series
nodes.description: Record simulator-generated carbon-dioxide volume at each stated timepoint.
hints: Keep time in seconds and gas volume in mL CO2.

nodes.title: Calculate the initial rate
nodes.description: Use the 0 s to 15 s secant slope and retain the mL CO2/s unit.
hints: Rate = change in gas volume divided by change in time.

feedback.retry: Use the early change in volume divided by 15 s.

nodes.title: Review evidence limits
nodes.description: Separate simulator output from physical measurements and identify why real trials require replicates.
hints: A deterministic curve contains no replicate scatter.

feedback.retry: Record provenance, repeatability needs, assumptions, and excluded effects.

successCriteria.label: Record evidence limits and repeatability needs.

commonMistakes.when: The reaction is initiated with a blocked or rigidly closed collection path.
commonMistakes.message: Gas generation in a rigid closed system can build unsafe pressure.
commonMistakes.recovery: Stop and restore the teacher-approved freely expanding or vented path.

commonMistakes.when: The timer is started after the defined reactant-contact event.
commonMistakes.message: Late timing biases the initial-rate calculation.
commonMistakes.recovery: Repeat with fresh configured reactants and synchronize timing to the defined contact event.

commonMistakes.when: The deterministic simulator series is described as student-measured replicate data.
commonMistakes.message: The guided series has no experimental scatter and cannot establish repeatability.
commonMistakes.recovery: Label simulator-generated data explicitly and use approved physical repeats for experimental variability.
